f.title: Apply E2A provisions together with other ICH GCP guidelines
f.statement: The provisions of the ICH E2A guideline on clinical safety data definitions and expedited reporting should be used in conjunction with the other ICH Good Clinical Practice guidelines.
f.clause: I. Introduction
f.applicability: Clinical safety data management during clinical development

rows.quote: The provisions of this guideline should be used in conjunction with other ICH Good Clinical Practice guidelines.
rows.location: I. Introduction

f.title: Treat any untoward medical occurrence after administration as an adverse event, regardless of causality
f.statement: An adverse event (or adverse experience) is any untoward medical occurrence in a patient or clinical investigation subject administered a pharmaceutical product, which does not necessarily have a causal relationship with the treatment. It can be any unfavourable and unintended sign (including an abnormal laboratory finding), symptom or disease temporally associated with use of a medicinal product, whether or not considered related to it.
f.clause: II.A.1. Adverse Event (or Adverse Experience)

rows.quote: Any untoward medical occurrence in a patient or clinical investigation subject administered a pharmaceutical product and which does not necessarily have to have a causal relationship with this treatment. An adverse event (AE) can therefore be any unfavourable and unintended sign (including an abnormal laboratory finding, for example), symptom, or disease temporally associated with the use of a medicinal product, whether or not considered related to the medicinal product.
rows.location: II.A.1. Adverse Event (or Adverse Experience)

f.title: Consider all noxious and unintended responses at any dose as ADRs in pre-approval clinical experience
f.statement: In the pre-approval clinical experience with a new medicinal product or its new usages, particularly where therapeutic doses may not be established, all noxious and unintended responses to a medicinal product related to any dose should be considered adverse drug reactions. "Responses to a medicinal product" means that a causal relationship between the product and the adverse event is at least a reasonable possibility, i.e. the relationship cannot be ruled out.
f.clause: II.A.2. Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR)
f.applicability: Pre-approval clinical experience with a new medicinal product or its new usages

rows.quote: In the pre-approval clinical experience with a new medicinal product or its new usages, particularly as the therapeutic dose(s) may not be established: all noxious and unintended responses to a medicinal product related to any dose should be considered adverse drug reactions. The phrase "responses to a medicinal products" means that a causal relationship between a medicinal product and an adverse event is at least a reasonable possibility, i.e., the relationship cannot be ruled out.
rows.location: II.A.2. Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR)
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: extended quote to the lead-in so it proves the pre-approval / dose-not-established condition; otherwise confirmed.

f.title: Use the WHO definition of an adverse drug reaction for marketed medicinal products
f.statement: For marketed medicinal products, the well-accepted post-marketing definition of an adverse drug reaction (WHO Technical Report 498, 1972) applies: a response to a drug which is noxious and unintended and which occurs at doses normally used in man for prophylaxis, diagnosis or therapy of disease or for modification of physiological function.
f.clause: II.A.2. Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR)
f.applicability: Marketed medicinal products, post-marketing setting

rows.quote: Regarding marketed medicinal products, a well-accepted definition of an adverse drug reaction in the post-marketing setting is found in WHO Technical Report 498 [1972] and reads as follows: A response to a drug which is noxious and unintended and which occurs at doses normally used in man for prophylaxis, diagnosis, or therapy of disease or for modification of physiological function.
rows.location: II.A.2. Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR)

f.title: Stop using the term "side effect" and do not treat it as synonymous with adverse event or reaction
f.statement: The term "side effect" should no longer be used and in particular should not be regarded as synonymous with adverse event or adverse reaction.
f.clause: II.A.2. Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR)

rows.quote: It is recommended that this term no longer be used and particularly should not be regarded as synonymous with adverse event or adverse reaction.
rows.location: II.A.2. Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR)

f.title: Classify an ADR as unexpected when its nature or severity is inconsistent with the applicable product information
f.statement: An unexpected adverse drug reaction is an adverse reaction whose nature or severity is not consistent with the applicable product information (e.g. the Investigator's Brochure for an unapproved investigational medicinal product).
f.clause: II.A.3. Unexpected Adverse Drug Reaction

rows.quote: An adverse reaction, the nature or severity of which is not consistent with the applicable product information (e.g., Investigator's Brochure for an unapproved investigational medicinal product).
rows.location: II.A.3. Unexpected Adverse Drug Reaction

f.title: Report reactions that threaten life or function promptly to regulators
f.statement: Adverse drug reactions occurring during clinical investigations that might be significant enough to lead to important changes in how the product is developed (e.g. dose, population, monitoring, consent forms), particularly reactions which in their most severe forms threaten life or function, should be reported promptly to regulators.
f.clause: II.B. Serious Adverse Event or Adverse Drug Reaction
f.applicability: Clinical investigations

rows.quote: During clinical investigations, adverse events may occur which, if suspected to be medicinal product-related (adverse drug reactions), might be significant enough to lead to important changes in the way the medicinal product is developed (e.g., change in dose, population, needed monitoring, consent forms). This is particularly true for reactions which, in their most severe forms, threaten life or function. Such reactions should be reported promptly to regulators.
rows.location: II.B. Serious Adverse Event or Adverse Drug Reaction
rows.review_note: Review: extended quote to the full paragraph so it proves the conditions (product-related events that may change development; dose, population, monitoring, consent forms) stated in the statement. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Base regulatory reporting on seriousness, not severity
f.statement: "Severe" describes the intensity of a specific event and is not synonymous with "serious", which is based on patient/event outcome or action criteria usually associated with events that threaten a patient's life or functioning. Seriousness (not severity) serves as the guide for defining regulatory reporting obligations.
f.clause: II.B. Serious Adverse Event or Adverse Drug Reaction

rows.quote: The term "severe" is often used to describe the intensity (severity) of a specific event (as in mild, moderate, or severe myocardial infarction); the event itself, however, may be of relatively minor medical significance (such as severe headache). This is not the same as "serious," which is based on patient/event outcome or action criteria usually associated with events that pose a threat to a patient's life or functioning. Seriousness (not severity) serves as a guide for defining regulatory reporting obligations.
rows.location: II.B. Serious Adverse Event or Adverse Drug Reaction
rows.review_note: Review: extended quote to include the definition of "severe" that the statement paraphrases. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Assess seriousness against the criteria of death, life-threatening, hospitalisation, disability and congenital anomaly
f.statement: A serious adverse event (experience) or reaction is any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose: results in death; is life-threatening (the patient was at risk of death at the time of the event, not an event that hypothetically might have caused death if more severe); requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalisation; results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity; or is a congenital anomaly/birth defect.
f.clause: II.B. Serious Adverse Event or Adverse Drug Reaction

rows.quote: A serious adverse event (experience) or reaction is any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose: * results in death, * is life-threatening, NOTE: The term "life-threatening" in the definition of "serious" refers to an event in which the patient was at risk of death at the time of the event; it does not refer to an event which hypothetically might have caused death if it were more severe. * requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalisation, * results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity, or * is a congenital anomaly/birth defect.
rows.location: II.B. Serious Adverse Event or Adverse Drug Reaction

f.title: Apply medical judgement to treat important medical events as serious for expedited reporting
f.statement: Medical and scientific judgement should be exercised in deciding whether expedited reporting is appropriate in other situations, such as important medical events that may not be immediately life-threatening or result in death or hospitalisation but may jeopardise the patient or require intervention to prevent one of the listed serious outcomes. These should usually also be considered serious (examples: intensive treatment in an emergency room or at home for allergic bronchospasm; blood dyscrasias or convulsions not resulting in hospitalisation; development of drug dependency or drug abuse).
f.clause: II.B. Serious Adverse Event or Adverse Drug Reaction

rows.quote: Medical and scientific judgement should be exercised in deciding whether expedited reporting is appropriate in other situations, such as important medical events that may not be immediately life-threatening or result in death or hospitalisation but may jeopardise the patient or may require intervention to prevent one of the other outcomes listed in the definition above. These should also usually be considered serious. Examples of such events are intensive treatment in an emergency room or at home for allergic bronchospasm; blood dyscrasias or convulsions that do not result in hospitalisation; or development of drug dependency or drug abuse.
rows.location: II.B. Serious Adverse Event or Adverse Drug Reaction
rows.review_note: Review: extended quote to include the examples cited in the statement. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Determine expectedness from previously observed information, not anticipated pharmacology
f.statement: Whether an adverse reaction is "expected" or "unexpected" is determined from the perspective of what has previously been observed, not on the basis of what might be anticipated from the pharmacological properties of the medicinal product.
f.clause: II.C. Expectedness of an Adverse Drug Reaction

f.title: Continue expedited reporting of additional occurrences of an unexpected reaction until source documents are amended
f.statement: An "unexpected" adverse reaction is one whose nature or severity is not consistent with the relevant source document(s). Until the source documents are amended, expedited reporting is required for additional occurrences of the reaction.
f.clause: II.C. Expectedness of an Adverse Drug Reaction
f.exceptions: Ends once the source document is amended to include the reaction

rows.quote: As stated in the definition (II.A.3.), an "unexpected" adverse reaction is one, the nature or severity of which is not consistent with information in the relevant source document(s). Until source documents are amended, expedited reporting is required for additional occurrences of the reaction.
rows.location: II.C. Expectedness of an Adverse Drug Reaction

f.title: Use the Investigator's Brochure as the expectedness reference for unapproved products
f.statement: For a medicinal product not yet approved for marketing in a country, the company's Investigator's Brochure serves as the source document for determining expectedness in that country.
f.clause: II.C. Expectedness of an Adverse Drug Reaction
f.applicability: Medicinal products not yet approved for marketing in the country concerned

rows.quote: For a medicinal product not yet approved for marketing in a country, a company's Investigator's Brochure will serve as the source document in that country.

f.title: Treat reports adding significant specificity or severity to a known serious ADR as unexpected
f.statement: Reports which add significant information on the specificity or severity of a known, already documented serious ADR constitute unexpected events; an event more specific or more severe than described in the Investigator's Brochure is considered unexpected (e.g. interstitial nephritis where acute renal failure is labelled; fulminant hepatitis where hepatitis is labelled).
f.clause: II.C. Expectedness of an Adverse Drug Reaction

rows.quote: Reports which add significant information on specificity or severity of a known, already documented serious ADR constitute unexpected events. For example, an event more specific or more severe than described in the Investigator's Brochure would be considered "unexpected". Specific examples would be (a) acute renal failure as a labeled ADR with a subsequent new report of interstitial nephritis and (b) hepatitis with a first report of fulminant hepatitis.
rows.location: II.C. Expectedness of an Adverse Drug Reaction
rows.review_note: Review: extended quote to include the interstitial nephritis and fulminant hepatitis examples given in the statement. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Expedite all serious and unexpected ADRs from any source
f.statement: All adverse drug reactions that are both serious and unexpected are subject to expedited reporting. This applies to reports from spontaneous sources and from any type of clinical or epidemiological investigation, independent of design or purpose, and to cases not reported directly to the sponsor or manufacturer (e.g. those found in regulatory authority-generated ADR registries or in publications).
f.clause: III.A.1. Single Cases of Serious, Unexpected ADRs
f.applicability: Spontaneous reports, clinical and epidemiological investigations, regulatory ADR registries and publications
f.processes: Reporting policy; Submission operations; Safety intake & collection

rows.quote: All adverse drug reactions (ADRs) that are both serious and unexpected are subject to expedited reporting. f.title: Do not ordinarily expedite serious expected reactions, unrelated serious study events or non-serious reactions
f.statement: Expedited reporting of reactions which are serious but expected will ordinarily be inappropriate. Expedited reporting is also inappropriate for serious events from clinical investigations considered not related to the study product, whether expected or not. Non-serious adverse reactions, whether expected or not, will ordinarily not be subject to expedited reporting.
f.clause: III.A.1. Single Cases of Serious, Unexpected ADRs

f.statement: Because there is no standard international nomenclature for causality, the expression "reasonable causal relationship" is meant to convey in general that there are facts (evidence) or arguments to suggest a causal relationship.

f.title: Communicate other safety observations that may alter benefit-risk or trial conduct rapidly to authorities
f.statement: Beyond single serious case reports, other situations may necessitate rapid communication to regulatory authorities, and appropriate medical and scientific judgement should be applied for each. In general these are information that might materially influence the benefit-risk assessment of a medicinal product or that would be sufficient to consider changes in product administration or in the overall conduct of a clinical investigation, e.g. a clinically important increase in the rate of an expected serious ADR, a significant hazard to the patient population such as lack of efficacy in life-threatening disease, or a major safety finding from a newly completed animal study (such as carcinogenicity).
f.clause: III.A.2. Other Observations
f.processes: Signal management; Submission operations; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote:
There are situations in addition to single case reports of "serious" adverse events or reactions that may necessitate rapid communication to regulatory authorities; appropriate medical and scientific judgement should be applied for each situation. In general, information that might materially influence the benefit-
risk assessment of a medicinal product or that would be sufficient to consider changes in medicinal product administration or in the overall conduct of a clinical investigation represents such situations. Examples include: a. For an "expected," serious ADR, an increase in the rate of occurrence which is judged to be clinically important. b. A significant hazard to the patient population, such as lack of efficacy with a medicinal product used in treating life-threatening disease. c. A major safety finding from a newly completed animal study (such as carcinogenicity).

f.title: Notify regulators of fatal or life-threatening unexpected ADRs from clinical investigations within 7 calendar days

Regulatory agencies in countries where the medicinal product, or its indication, formulation or population, is not yet approved for marketing should be notified (e.g. by telephone, facsimile transmission or in writing) as soon as possible but no later than 7 calendar days after first knowledge by the sponsor that a case qualifies.

f.title: Break the blind for the specific patient when a serious reaction is expedited-reportable
f.statement: When the sponsor and investigator are blinded to individual patient treatment (as in a double-blind study), the occurrence of a serious event requires a decision on whether to open (break) the code for that patient. If the investigator breaks the blind, it is assumed the sponsor will also know the assigned treatment. Although it is advantageous to retain the blind for all patients prior to final study analysis, when a serious adverse reaction is judged reportable on an expedited basis, the blind should be broken by the sponsor only for that specific patient, even if the investigator has not broken the blind.
f.clause: III.D. Managing Blinded Therapy Cases
f.applicability: Blinded (e.g. double-blind) clinical studies
f.exceptions: See the exception for studies where a fatal or serious outcome is the primary efficacy endpoint
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: When the sponsor and investigator are blinded to individual patient treatment (as in a double-blind study), the occurrence of a serious event requires a decision on whether to open (break) the code for the specific patient. Although it is advantageous to retain the blind for all patients prior to final study analysis, when a serious adverse reaction is judged reportable on an expedited basis, it is recommended that the blind be broken only for that specific patient by the sponsor even if the investigator has not broken the blind.

f.statement: It is the sponsor's responsibility to decide whether active comparator drug reactions should be reported to the other manufacturer and/or directly to the appropriate regulatory agencies.

f.title: Report or reference an expedited ADR across all other presentations and uses of the product
f.statement: To avoid ambiguities and uncertainties, an ADR that qualifies for expedited reporting with one presentation of a product (e.g. dosage form, formulation, delivery system) or product use (e.g. indication or population) should be reported or referenced to regulatory filings across the other product presentations and uses.

f.title: Cover ADR information for all presentations and uses in each Investigator's Brochure
f.statement: Because expectedness may be product- or use-specific, separate Investigator's Brochures may be used for different presentations or uses. f.title: Treat post-study serious adverse events as study reports for expedited reporting
f.statement: Serious adverse events occurring after the patient has completed a clinical study (including any protocol-required post-treatment follow-up) that are reported by an investigator to the sponsor should be regarded, for expedited reporting purposes, as though they were study reports. A causality assessment and determination of expectedness are therefore needed to decide whether expedited reporting is required.
f.clause: III.E.3. Post-study Events
f.applicability: Serious adverse events occurring after the patient completed a clinical study (including protocol-required post-treatment follow-up) that an investigator reports to the sponsor; such information is not routinely sought or collected by the sponsor
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Medical review; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: Although such information is not routinely sought or collected by the sponsor, serious adverse events that occurred after the patient had completed a clinical study (including any protocol-required post-treatment follow-up) will possibly be reported by an investigator to the sponsor. Such cases should be regarded for expedited reporting purposes as though they were study reports. Therefore, a causality assessment and determination of expectedness are needed for a decision on whether or not expedited reporting is required.

f.title: Ensure the minimum information for expedited reporting is present
f.statement: The minimum information required for expedited reporting purposes is: an identifiable patient, the name of a suspect medicinal product, an identifiable reporting source, and an event or outcome that can be identified as serious and unexpected and for which, in clinical investigation cases, there is a reasonable suspected causal relationship.
f.clause: Attachment 1. Key Data Elements for Inclusion in Expedited Reports of Serious Adverse Drug Reactions

f.title: Capture patient details in expedited reports
f.statement: Expedited reports of serious ADRs should include, where available and relevant, patient details: initials; other relevant identifier (e.g. clinical investigation number); gender; age and/or date of birth; weight; height.
f.clause: Attachment 1, 1. Patient Details

f.title: Capture suspected medicinal product details in expedited reports
f.statement: Expedited reports should include, where available, for each suspected medicinal product: brand name as reported; International Non-Proprietary Name (INN); batch number; indication(s) for which it was prescribed or tested; dosage form and strength; daily dose and regimen (with units); route of administration; starting date and time of day; stopping date and time, or duration of treatment.
f.clause: Attachment 1, 2. Suspected Medicinal Product(s)

rows.location: Attachment 1, 2. Suspected Medicinal Product(s)

f.title: Provide the same details for concomitant products and non-drug therapies
f.statement: For concomitant medicinal products (including non-prescription/OTC products) and non-medicinal product therapies, the same information as for the suspected product should be provided.
f.clause: Attachment 1, 3. Other Treatment(s)

rows.quote: For concomitant medicinal products (including non-prescription/OTC medicinal products) and non-medicinal product therapies, provide the same information as for the suspected product.

f.title: Describe the reaction fully, state the seriousness criteria and seek a specific diagnosis
f.statement: A full description of the reaction(s), including body site and severity, and the criterion (or criteria) for regarding the report as serious should be given. In addition to describing the reported signs and symptoms, attempts should be made whenever possible to establish a specific diagnosis for the reaction.
f.clause: Attachment 1, 4. Details of Suspected Adverse Drug Reaction(s)

f.title: Capture reaction timing, dechallenge/rechallenge, setting and outcome
f.statement: Expedited reports should include the start date (and time) of onset of the reaction, stop date (and time) or duration, dechallenge and rechallenge information, setting (e.g. hospital, out-patient clinic, home, nursing home), and outcome: information on recovery and any sequelae, and what specific tests and/or treatment may have been required and their results.

f.title: Provide cause of death, relationship comment and post-mortem findings for fatal cases
f.statement: For a fatal outcome, the cause of death and a comment on its possible relationship to the suspected reaction should be provided. Any autopsy or other post-mortem findings (including a coroner's report) should also be provided when available.

f.statement: Expedited reports should include administrative and sponsor/company details: source of report (spontaneous, clinical investigation with details, literature with a copy, other); date the event report was first received by the sponsor/manufacturer; country in which the event occurred; type of report filed (initial or follow-up, and which follow-up); name and address of the sponsor/manufacturer/company; name, address, telephone and fax number of the contact person in the reporting company or institution; and the identifying regulatory code or number for the marketing authorisation dossier or clinical investigation process (e.g. IND, CTX or NDA number).
